title: EventEnvelope
description: An immutable fact that has already occurred. Events are written in the same transaction as the state change that produced them (transactional outbox, docs/05, ADR-006).

event_id.description: Unique identity of this event. Prefix evt_.

aggregate_type.description: Type of the aggregate whose state changed.

aggregate_id.description: Identity of the aggregate. Type-appropriate prefixed identifier.

causation_id.description: The command or event that directly caused this event. Null only for a root event.

producer_id.description: The single owning component that produced this event. Exactly one owner per authoritative fact (docs/01, docs/25 §2).

occurred_at.description: When the fact occurred in the owning domain.

recorded_at.description: When the platform durably recorded the fact. recorded_at >= occurred_at is not assumed; clock skew is measured, not hidden.

source_timestamp.description: Vendor or venue supplied timestamp where one exists. Never trusted without a freshness and clock-skew check (docs/16).

sequence.description: Monotonic per-aggregate sequence. A gap or duplicate is a detectable anomaly, never silently tolerated (docs/01 §8).

allOf.$comment: aggregate_type must agree with the aggregate_id prefix. This is enforced by the schema, not left to a binding convention.
config_snapshot, reconciliation_case, feed, dataset, and experiment share the run_/evt_ identifier space; their bindings add the narrower check.

x-invariants: Events are immutable. A correction is a new compensating event; an event is never edited or deleted (docs/04, docs/05).
Delivery is at-least-once. Consumers MUST be idempotent. No exactly-once assumption is made anywhere (ADR-020, docs/25 §6).
A duplicate delivery must never cause a duplicate domain transition (docs/09 invariant 3).
An event is written in the same transaction as the state change. A committed state change with no event, or an event with no state change, is a defect.
Events carry no authority by themselves. Authority lives in the owning module's state, not in the event log.
